extraction_notes: report_status/report_reason are mirrored from data/snapshots/injuries-2026-11-16-0915am.json by (report_block, report_name) join at build time and were re-verified against it row for row (57/57); they are the report's printed cells, not this file's observations.

Verbatim rule: a player with a game in the window appears either with a printed stat line (MIN/PTS/REB/AST as printed strings; REB is the printed TOT column, AST the printed A column) or with the printed designation (Inactive list entry, DNP - Coach's Decision, DND -- ...). No value was computed or inferred.
Every row cites its own gamebook URL in source_url; game_id values are the ones recorded in data/snapshots/results-2026-11-14.json from the official game pages.

Name matching between the report's 'Last, First' print and the gamebook's 'First Last' print is by exact name tokens; suffixes (Jr., II, III) are kept as printed on both sides. One spelling variance surfaced: the gamebook inactive list prints 'Mobely' where the report prints 'Mobley, Evan' (flag SP-01); both spellings are kept as printed.

The 7 injury-report rows whose team cell was lost at a page break keep a blank team in the injury snapshot; here their game-log rows carry the team from the gamebook's own team header (attribution_note on each row). This does not repair the injury row.

Golden State block rows: Butler III prints a reason and no status; Curry/Moody/Porzingis/Santos/Williams print a status and no reason (one status-or-reason cell per row). The missing cells stay blank on both the report side and here.

The report prints 'Reese, Julian' and 'Watford, Trendon' among the GSW@NOP lost rows; the DEN@NOP gamebook prints 'Julian Reese' (DNP - Coach's Decision) and 'Watford' on the Pelicans inactive list with the same Right Ankle Sprain reason as the report row. Both rows are attributed to the Pelicans from the gamebook, not from the report.
